text:
samir: Heads up — saw a spike of GPU pods stuck PENDING in us-central1-a this morning. quota looks normal but nodepools didn't scale fast enough.
ciara: Which pool? link to the pending list: https://redwood.internal/queue/3172
autoscaler-bot: scale event: requested 8 nodes for pool-gpu-preemptible-us-central1 at 1719005000; 3 nodes returned, remaining 5 pending quota in zone 'a'
alex: Seems CA is favoring preemptible nodes (cheapest). When preemptibles hit quota we end up with lots of pending pods and slow cross-zone rebalancing.
kevin: Are we still using --expander=lowest-price? that explains the chase across zones.
samir: Yep. Current policy was to minimize $/token but latency-critical workloads are getting starved.
ciara: Quick idea: introduce a "soft-reservation" label on a fraction of nodes per zone to guarantee some non-preemptible capacity for realtime class. Not a full dedicated pool, just reserved capacity.
alex: I like that. Also change CA tuning: reduce scaleDownUnneededTime and add a zone-preference expander so we avoid moving across regions unless absolutely necessary.
kevin: Cost hit estimate: reserving 20% of GPU capacity as non-preemptible increases spend, rough calc: delta ~$0.5/hr per GPU * 40 GPUs = ~$20/hr. Need exact numbers but manageable for high-priority SLAs.
samir: Alternate mitigation: better ingress backpressure + degraded model fallback when GPUs unavailable. Queue & probe approach buys us time without permanently reserving nodes.
ciara: Proposal steps: 1) feature-flag soft-reserve labels on 20% of each zone 2) CA expander -> prefer-labeled-nodes then lowest-price 3) run a probe job to simulate high allocation across zones 4) add pending-gpu alerts and cost delta spreadsheet
alex: Snippet for nodeSelector and CA flag to try in staging:
```
# node template for soft-reserve small pool
nodeSelector:
  redwood/instance-class: realtime
# CA flags
--expander=most-pods 
--balance-similar-node-groups
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
```
kevin: Who will run the probe and collect metrics (time-to-provision, scheduling-delay, cross-zone-allocs)?
ops-oncall: I can run the probe. prefer overnight low-traffic window.
samir: Let's run probe at 03:00 UTC tomorrow. I'll open the PR for label rollout and a small bash probe harness.
ciara: I'll put the plan in the runbook and add an RFC link. Also will add a quick cost model spreadsheet.
alex: Add alerts: pending-gpu-duration > 300s and pods-scheduled-to-preemptible > threshold. Tie to eng-oncall.
autoscaler-bot: alert created: pending-gpu-duration > 300s -> #eng-oncall (alert-id: A-2026033)
kevin: :thumbsup: After probe we'll decide between soft-reserve and model-fallback flow. keep both options on the table.
ops-oncall: noted. I'll push probe results and raw timings to the thread after run.
samir: Cool. Action items: samir -> PR for labels, ciara -> runbook + cost sheet, ops-oncall -> run probe at 03:00 UTC, alex -> CA flag experiment in staging. Thanks all.
ciara: :rocket:
